html:
The Terengganu Inscription Stone, found at Kuala Berang in Terengganu, is the oldest known Malay text in Jawi, the Arabic script for Malay. It is usually dated to 1303.

It records a ruler's order to uphold Islam and sets out Islamic laws and punishments, using a mix of Malay and Arabic words with some Sanskrit. It shows Islam as the law of a Malay state more than a century before the rise of Malacca.

The stone came to light in the late 19th century and is a national treasure. It marks the start of the Islamic Malay world that later took shape under Malacca and then the Johor and other sultanates. See also Arabic script.
